headlines.title: Fed delivers its first hike in 3 years. Plus, what's moving Starbucks and GE Vernova
headlines.summary: The Fed just pulled the trigger on its first rate hike in three years — that's the tape-mover of the decade, folks. Every sector from housing to tech to financials reprices when the cost of money shifts, and with Warsh signaling more tightening ahead, the long bond is going to stay under pressure. Trump's already jawboning about 1% rates, which adds a political wildcard that keeps volatility elevated across the board.

headlines.title: Amazon obtains right to buy stock in Generac, boosting power company's share price by over 40%
headlines.summary: Amazon just handed Generac a $340 million warrant deal tied to data center backup power — and the stock ripped 40% on the news, which is about as clean a single-name catalyst as you'll see. This validates the AI infrastructure power-demand thesis in a big way, and it puts every other backup power and energy equipment name in play as the Street scrambles to find the next Generac. Watch the whole power-generation complex light up.

headlines.title: Number of ships transiting Strait of Hormuz falls to three on Wednesday, data shows
headlines.summary: Three ships through the Strait of Hormuz — that's not a shipping lane, that's a parking lot. About 20% of the world's oil flows through that chokepoint, and when traffic drops to near-zero, every energy trader on the floor is watching crude, LNG, and tanker rates like a hawk. Saudi pipeline restoration is offering some relief, but this remains the single biggest supply-shock risk keeping oil elevated and bond markets on edge.
